chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Abdullah Al-A'raj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the charity permissible for the mawalis (clients/freedmen) of Banu Hashim?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.مَوَالِي: Clients/Freedmen (those connected to a tribe through manumission or alliance)

ai.seo_question: Are the mawalis of Banu Hashim eligible to receive sadaqah?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that the mawalis (clients or freedmen) of Banu Hashim are eligible to receive sadaqah, distinguishing them from the Banu Hashim themselves who are generally prohibited from receiving it due to their status as recipients of khums. This ruling highlights the nuanced application of almsgiving rules within the Prophet’s lineage, ensuring that those connected to the clan through patronage or manumission are not excluded from charitable support.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Saeed Bin Abdullah Al A’araj who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is the charity Permissible for the slave of the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Sa‘id ibn ‘Abd Allah al-A‘raj who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
Is charity lawful for Mawali (servants) of children of al-Hashim?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, it is lawful.’”
